answer: Decaying reputation bridge.** Each identity carries a reputation score earned through verified transactions, and to spawn a new identity an agent must transfer a fraction of its own score as an origin endowment. That transfer decays: the donor loses more than the recipient gains, with the gap widening as scores diverge. An attacker running N clones must therefore bleed score from a real, earned base for every unit added, so the cost curve steepens with each clone. A shared atlas of transaction history anchors scores, and a lotus multiplier rewards long-lived identities,
